Hi! We use am, is and are every day. Look: Sara is kind. Sara is she, so we say is. Use am with I, is with he, she or it, and are with we, you or they. Right: He is kind. Wrong: He are kind. Your turn! Write am, is or are: The cat ___ small.

Hi! A and an come before one thing. Look: I see an egg. Use a before a consonant sound, and an before a vowel sound (a, e, i, o, u). Right: I see an ant. Wrong: I see a ant. Your turn! Write a or an: I see ___ owl.

Hi! We can talk about finished actions with the past. Look: Yesterday I cooked dinner. The action is finished, so cook becomes cooked. Rule: add -ed to a regular verb to talk about a finished action.
Right: Yesterday she jumped.
Wrong: Yesterday she jump.
Your turn! Write the past: Yesterday we ___ (clean) the room.
